title: Vaginal Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Vaginal Cancer. Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (pelvic speculum and bimanual rectovaginal EUA mapping tumor epicenter and distance from introitus, biopsy confirming primary invasive vaginal carcinoma with cervical primary excluded, high-resolution pelvic MRI with contrast, whole-body FDG-PET/CT or contrast CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, cystoscopy and proctosigmoidoscopy for stage II or higher disease abutting anterior or posterior wall, biomarker testing for PD-L1 CPS, MMR/MSI, and high-risk HPV) -> FIGO Stage Stratification (Stage I confined to vaginal wall vs Stage II-IVa locoregionally advanced with paravaginal, pelvic sidewall, or regional nodal disease vs Stage IVb distant metastatic or incurable recurrent) -> Stage I local therapy (radical vaginectomy or radical hysterectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy for upper-third favorable surgical candidates, or definitive EBRT plus image-guided brachytherapy for most patients) -> Locoregionally advanced definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (pelvic EBRT with weekly cisplatin followed by interstitial or intracavitary IGBT boost) -> Metastatic first-line systemic chemoimmunotherapy (platinum plus paclitaxel plus pembrolizumab with or without bevacizumab per KEYNOTE-826 extrapolated data; second-line tisotumab vedotin or pembrolizumab monotherapy for MSI-H, TMB-H, or PD-L1 CPS >=1). References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Vaginal Cancer Version 2.2026.

a.text: Primary vaginal carcinoma requires exclusion of cervical primary extension: tumor epicenter must map to the vagina with no gross cervical involvement, and pathology must confirm invasive vaginal histology (squamous cell carcinoma in over 80% of cases, adenocarcinoma, clear cell carcinoma, or melanoma).

b.text: High-resolution pelvic MRI with contrast is optimal for depth of paravaginal invasion, pelvic sidewall involvement, and bladder or rectal wall abutment; whole-body FDG-PET/CT stages regional lymphadenopathy and distant metastases. Cystoscopy and proctosigmoidoscopy apply to stage II or higher tumors abutting the anterior or posterior vaginal wall.

c.text: Stage I definitive radiotherapy: pelvic EBRT 45 Gy followed by image-guided brachytherapy (intracavitary cylinder or interstitial needle implant) to a cumulative EQD2 of at least 70-75 Gy to the primary tumor volume.

d.text: Locoregionally advanced definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy: pelvic EBRT 45-50.4 Gy (add bilateral inguinofemoral nodal fields when the lower third of the vagina is involved) with concurrent weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV during EBRT for 5-6 doses, followed by interstitial or intracavitary IGBT boost to cumulative EQD2 of at least 80-85 Gy; boost PET-positive nodes to 60-66 Gy.

e.text: Metastatic first-line systemic therapy extrapolates KEYNOTE-826 cervical data: cisplatin 50 mg/m2 (or carboplatin AUC 4-5) plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 plus pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks (or 400 mg every 6 weeks) with or without bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks; second-line options are tisotumab vedotin 2.0 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (antibody-drug conjugate) or pembrolizumab monotherapy for MSI-H, TMB-H, or PD-L1 CPS >=1 disease.

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Vaginal Cancer: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Step 1: Complete the clinical workup before FIGO stage stratification. Map the tumor epicenter, confirm primary invasive vaginal histology with cervical primary excluded, stage local and distant extent with MRI and PET/CT, scope adjacent organs for stage II or higher disease, and test predictive biomarkers.
bullets: Careful pelvic speculum and bimanual rectovaginal examination under anesthesia (EUA) mapping exact tumor epicenter and distance from introitus
Biopsy confirming primary invasive vaginal carcinoma (squamous cell carcinoma >80%, adenocarcinoma, clear cell, melanoma) while excluding cervical primary extension
High-resolution pelvic MRI with contrast (optimal for depth of paravaginal invasion, pelvic sidewall, and bladder/rectal involvement)
Whole-body FDG-PET/CT (or CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast) to assess regional lymphadenopathy and distant metastatic disease
Cystoscopy and proctosigmoidoscopy for stage II or higher tumors abutting the anterior or posterior vaginal wall
Biomarker testing on tumor tissue: PD-L1 IHC (CPS), MMR/MSI, and high-risk HPV testing

options.label: Workup Complete - Proceed to FIGO Stage Stratification

nodes.name: FIGO Stage Stratification
nodes.title: Vaginal Cancer: FIGO Stage Stratification
nodes.description: Workup complete. Assign FIGO stage from confinement to the vaginal wall, paravaginal or pelvic sidewall extension, regional nodal status, and distant spread; the group selects the Stage I local-therapy, locoregionally advanced chemoradiotherapy, or metastatic systemic-therapy pathway.
bullets: FIGO Stage I: tumor confined strictly to the vaginal wall or mucosa with no paravaginal extension.

FIGO Stage II-IVa locoregionally advanced: paravaginal tissue involvement, pelvic sidewall extension, bladder or rectal mucosal involvement without fistula beyond vagina, or regional lymph node involvement.
FIGO Stage IVb distant metastatic or incurable recurrent: spread beyond the pelvis to distant organs or non-regional nodes, or recurrence not amenable to curative local therapy.

options.label: FIGO Stage I Vaginal Cancer (Confined strictly to vaginal wall / mucosa)
FIGO Stage II-IVa Locoregionally Advanced Vaginal Cancer (Paravaginal, pelvic sidewall, or regional nodes)
Distant Metastatic or Incurable Recurrent Vaginal Cancer (FIGO Stage IVb)

nodes.name: Stage I Treatment
nodes.title: Stage I: Radical Vaginectomy or Definitive EBRT Plus Brachytherapy
nodes.description: Local therapy for FIGO Stage I disease confined to the vagina: radical surgery for favorable upper-third surgical candidates, or definitive EBRT plus image-guided brachytherapy as standard for most patients.
bullets: Upper 1/3 vagina (favorable surgical candidate): radical vaginectomy or radical hysterectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy.

Definitive radiotherapy (standard for most patients): external beam radiation therapy (EBRT: 45 Gy to pelvis) plus image-guided brachytherapy (IGBT: intracavitary cylinder or interstitial needle implant delivering cumulative EQD2 >=70-75 Gy).
Select surgical candidates by upper-vaginal location, small tumor size, and fitness for radical pelvic surgery with lymphadenectomy; all others proceed to definitive radiotherapy.
Surveillance after definitive local therapy: pelvic examination with speculum and bimanual rectovaginal assessment plus cross-sectional imaging for symptoms or high-risk pathology.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Radical Vaginectomy or Definitive EBRT (45 Gy) + Image-Guided Brachytherapy (IGBT)

nodes.name: Locoregionally Advanced Treatment
nodes.title: Stage II-IVa: Definitive Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy Plus IGBT
nodes.description: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locoregionally advanced vaginal cancer: pelvic EBRT with weekly cisplatin followed by interstitial or intracavitary IGBT boost, with nodal boost for PET-positive lymph nodes.
bullets: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy: pelvic EBRT (45-50.4 Gy to pelvis; add bilateral inguinofemoral nodal fields if lower 1/3 vagina involved) with concurrent weekly cisplatin (40 mg/m2 IV weekly during EBRT x 5-6 doses).
Follow EBRT with interstitial or intracavitary image-guided brachytherapy (IGBT boost achieving cumulative EQD2 >=80-85 Gy to primary tumor volume).
Nodal boost to 60-66 Gy for PET-positive lymph nodes.
Monitor renal function, audiologic status, and hematologic counts on weekly cisplatin; coordinate across gynecologic oncology, medical oncology, and radiation oncology.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Definitive Concurrent ChemoRT (Pelvic EBRT + Weekly Cisplatin 40 mg/m2) + Interstitial IGBT

nodes.name: Metastatic Treatment
nodes.title: Stage IVb: First-Line Systemic Chemoimmunotherapy Then ADC or Pembrolizumab
nodes.description: First-line platinum, paclitaxel, and pembrolizumab with or without bevacizumab for distant metastatic or incurable recurrent vaginal cancer, followed by tisotumab vedotin or pembrolizumab monotherapy for biomarker-selected disease.
bullets: First-line systemic chemoimmunotherapy: cisplatin 50 mg/m2 (or carboplatin AUC 4-5) plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 plus pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w (or 400 mg q6w) with or without bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w (KEYNOTE-826 data).
Second-line: tisotumab vedotin 2.0 mg/kg IV q3w (antibody-drug conjugate, ADC) or pembrolizumab monotherapy (for MSI-H, TMB-H, or PD-L1 CPS >=1).
Establish PD-L1 CPS, MMR/MSI, TMB, and high-risk HPV status at diagnosis of metastatic disease to set immunotherapy eligibility; offer clinical trial enrollment at every line.

Stage with cross-sectional imaging at baseline and every 8-12 weeks on systemic therapy; monitor for immune-related adverse events on pembrolizumab and ocular, bleeding, and neuropathy signals on tisotumab vedotin.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
